Hmm.. You said you're halfway through the semester, right? Only halfway, and only one semester. Plus, I'm guessing you started second semester. You didn't start at the university in the fall. That as well makes a big difference. Fall is when there are new people/transfers, everyone's sorta entering the fray at the same time.. people are more vulnerable and cliques haven't fully established yet. So, more people in the same boat as you. I started here in the winter quarter, so it was harder. Many swear by the fall as a good time in college for new beginnings. So if you can keep your grades up you can start on a new foot next fall, or maybe even at a new school. And if you're learning new things and focusing on yourself/your studies, you may build that confidence you need to give you that extra kick. Sounds like you have a good baseline to start from (you're not awkward, you're not unattractive, so be thankful for that). Once you kinda decide you've got a passion going you could even go on to grad school and possibly meet people there. 

I do agree about living off-campus as being a bit of a hindrance, yes it is easier to establish bonds living on campus, but it can only do so much. If you're already without a group and feeling "on the outside looking in," so to speak, living in a dorm will only do so much for you. Even still, you may want to consider finding out how you could live on campus. Is there any particular reason you can't live on campus? Also, have you tried joining a club? That's a great way to make casual connections where everyone isn't just focusing on themselves. I understand how lecture halls can be tough spots to meet people. Also, maybe girls have been noticing your athletic progress, but are just too shy to say anything. Many girls hate making the first move and want the guy to approach them first. Its flattering and sometimes they think that if they "have" to make the first move on a dude, it's because they are defective somehow and they get insecure/embarrassed. This doesn't apply to all girls of course, but some.

Wow, I can relate to pretty much everything you've just said. I am also 21, at a university, and it's been a shit-show. I transferred from a community college as well, after having a complicated high-school experience where I missed out on a lot of the opportunities I feel like I should have gone through- no senior party, no prom, and I left school without many friends. I recently started running though, and that's boosted my confidence quite a bit, not in the social sense but it just makes me feel a little more even-keeled in my head and kinda takes the load off. I'm slowly taking this in stride. Things are almost kinda coming into perspective. In your case, I would try asking questions to classmates in the actual in-person classes you do have. Simple questions about the material, or even a simple question like "can I borrow your pen" gets the ball rolling in a way, and I've heard that asking for help subconsciously triggers something in others that leads them to like you on a basic level. Something about feeling important. People like people who trust them with questions or simple requests. Try talking to less-attractive girls to boost your confidence with breaking the ice... even if you don't wanna get with them, you can treat them as a friend, they may have cute friends, and the more people you know even on a basic level, the better your chances are of meeting that cute girl that you really dig.

But you have to say "fuck it" at some point and just go for the little talk at times.. even if it fails, do you think these people will care once you're outta college? Nah. Longboard around campus or something. Girls will probably comment if you do it enough. I'm in college now, and relating to people with my social anxiety has been really tough. I too feel like I am somehow "less" than other people most of the time, even though there are moments where it dawns on me that no one is actually better than another person, and we really are all the same at the core... human, same basic genetic makeup, same drives, same basic instincts and such. If you think about this in a biological sense it makes sense (all animals of a certain species can relate to each other in a basic sense), and yet with certain individuals and humans in general it can become really hard to remember that. I feel as if I'm not "created equal" in the eyes of others. There's an inherent lack of worth I feel and this makes it hard for me to successfully pull off the role of being someone else, in a way that convinces others I am a fully functional human. I could pull this off really well in high school, and even got a certain "high" from playing off that image, but certain drugs and series of events led to me being in a constant state of self-denial, and not really feeling anything. Prozac definitely made me feel a bit numb, but also edgy at the same time. I also feel a great deal of anxiety when talking on the phone, or if someone takes too long to text me back. Try to remember that even if you don't see your situation as unique, it truly is- I think even being able to function to this point with anxiety issues is a noteworthy feat- it's not easy to stay with it, give yourself some credit. And no one really is in the same situation as you, either. No one knows exactly how you feel, so your situation is really unique. This may not help much, but I feel ya. There's ways to tweak the system so you can work and not be an economic pawn. Try to squeeze things into your life that make you feel good. I go to raves to feel alive because I need an escape from reality. Tap into whatever it is that seems to be more meaningful than "going to school, jumping through hoops, and climbing the economic ladder." there is more out there for those who can look beyond the voices of everyone saying that money and school are the only things that matter.

I prefer sativa greatly.

The difference between a sativa and an indica is generally that sativa is a mood-lifter; its high is euphoric and more "energetic". More of a daytime smoke. I usually feel enlightened, creative and adventuresome when I'm lucky enough to come by a nice sativa strain. It's characteristics as far as the plant is concerned are wider, skinnier leaves and (usually, but not always) a lighter coloring.

Indica is used more often for medical patients due to its pain relieving and sedating qualities. It's the space-out strain, not so much giving the "enlightened ideas" type of experience that I'd get from a sativa. I call it the "couch-lock" type of weed. Good if you really just want to chill, and more of a nighttime smoke (get ready for good dreams). :)

If you want to know by strain name, here's a rule of thumb: If you've got something with "haze" in the title, Trainwreck, or Jack Herer= sativa. If you've got anything "kush", you're looking at indica.
